title: 2011 AMC 12B Problem 19
statement: A lattice point in an \(xy\)-coordinate system is any point \((x, y)\) where both \(x\) and \(y\) are integers. The graph of \(y=mx+2\) passes through no lattice point with \(0 \lt x \le 100\) for all \(m\) such that \(\dfrac{1}{2} \lt m \lt a.\) What is the maximum possible value of \(a?\)

solutions.text:
For \(0\lt x\le100,\) the nearest lattice point above the line \(y=\tfrac12x+2\) is \(\left(x,\tfrac12x+3\right)\) if \(x\) is even and \(\left(x,\tfrac12x+\tfrac52\right)\) if \(x\) is odd.

The slope from \((0,2)\) to that point is \(\dfrac12+\dfrac1x\) for even \(x\) and \(\dfrac12+\dfrac{1}{2x}\) for odd \(x.\) The minimum such slope is \(\dfrac{51}{100}\) for even \(x\) and \(\dfrac{50}{99}\) for odd \(x.\)

Since \(\dfrac{50}{99}\lt\dfrac{51}{100},\) the line avoids all these lattice points exactly when \(\dfrac12\lt m\lt\dfrac{50}{99},\) so the maximum is \(a=\dfrac{50}{99}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: For each \(x,\) find the smallest slope \(\gt\dfrac12\) from \((0,2)\) that reaches a lattice point at that \(x\)
Compare the minimum slopes for even \(x\) and odd \(x;\) the tighter bound wins
